notes: Electric-dryer parts from the Samsung DV45H Series service manual, which covers DV45H* and DV42H* dryers; the DV42H5000* wiring diagram is named but the EW suffix is not printed. The 5300 W heater rating is from the DV45H*/DV42H* family table.

gaps: The manual's cover line is DV45H* DV42H*, and wiring diagram 6-3 is titled DV42H5400*, DV42H5200*, DV42H5000*; the full model DV42H5000EW (with suffix) is not printed, so it is covered only by those wildcards.
The 5300 W (Elec.) heater rating is from the DV45H*, DV42H* family spec table on page 8, not a table for this model alone.
Heater resistance readings on page 37 (dual-element 13 and 34 Ω, single-element 10 Ω) are not tied to this model, so left out; the separate heating_element_coil claim was merged into heating_element.
Thermostat roles (high limit or cycling) are not labelled on page 37, so the three thermostats stay numbered.
The rating table at the foot of page 37 (85 C 25 A thermal cut-off, 125 V 10 A, 125 V 15 A, lamp) is not paired reliably by the text order, so none of it is used.
No thermal fuse, blower wheel, timer, moisture sensor or motor rating on the pages read; no part numbers because the pages read have no parts list.
No production years are given for this model.
method: Samsung DV45H Series Service Manual (ManualsLib manual 1895735, 46 pages) read through the ManualsLib viewer: cover and contents page for the model list, then viewer pages 5, 8, 33 and 37.
Page 5 is the electrical service information. Page 8 is the specifications table. Page 33 is the drum-does-not-turn flowchart. Page 37 is component testing with an ohmmeter.
No bot check, login wall or paywall on any page read.
The DV42H technical data sheet (ManualsLib manual 718909) is a separate document and is not cited.
manualshive.com (bot check) and manualmachine.com (HTTP 403) refused the researcher and are not cited.

comps.spec: Electric heater, rated 5300 W (Elec.) in the specifications table for DV45H* and DV42H* dryers.

Three thermostats tested for continuity with an ohmmeter: No. 1 (white and yellow wires), No. 2 (blue and black) and No. 3 (red and black), each under 1 Ω when good. The page says to replace No. 2 or No. 3 if it reads infinite.
Thermistor, 10 kΩ at 25 °C (77 °F), on a two-pin connector with blue and red wires.
Door switch. With the knob open, COM to NC (pins 1-3) reads below 1 Ω and COM to NO (pins 1-2) reads open. The readings reverse when the switch is pushed.
Belt cut-off switch. Below 1 Ω with the lever open, open (∞) with the lever pushed.
Drive motor. The drum-does-not-turn check names the motor, its motor protector and the centrifugal switch as the things to check.
Drum belt and idler, named together with the drive motor in the drum-does-not-turn check.
PCB assembly. The drum-does-not-turn flowchart names it as the part to replace once the motor checks pass.

Power cord of the electric dryer (the safety page says not to modify its plug or pinch it). The electrical service information for electric dryers is 240 VAC, 60 Hz, 30 A, for 3-wire or 4-wire installations.
